findings.mechanism: Each Hub.Open starts a per-subscription worker goroutine (run) with a 4KiB scratch buffer, which would accumulate if Close were skipped.
findings.cause: Suspected unclosed subscription workers; ruled out.
findings.evidence: Read all code: the only Open caller, Handler.Serve (handler.go:178-182), does `defer sub.Close()` right after Open, so every return path (including Push/Flush errors) closes done and waits on exited; run() returns on done. Ran a scratch copy (outside the source tree) replaying 5x20000 requests with GC after each batch: goroutines stayed at 2 every batch; HeapAlloc 134KB->159KB and HeapObjects 486->575 over 100k requests, which is noise rather than per-request growth. Existing go test ./... passes.
findings.discriminator: Goroutine count is flat (2) after every batch and heap objects do not scale with requests; Serve defers Close on all paths.

findings.mechanism: MemorySink keeps state across all requests.
findings.cause: Suspected unbounded retention in the sink; ruled out.
findings.evidence: MemorySink stores only int counters and a uint32 checksum, no slices or maps; Renderer layouts map is copied once at construction and fixed size. Heap object count flat in the measurement above.
